# nonEmptyString

<link-summary>Returns the value as a non-empty string, naming the argument in the failure.</link-summary>

<web-summary>nonEmptyString() — Returns the value as a non-empty string, naming the argument in the failure. apps-script-utils, English.</web-summary>

<tldr>
<p>Module: <code>lang/string</code> · Since: 1.5.0 · <b>Deprecated</b></p>
</tldr>

> **Deprecated.** Use [`requireNonEmptyString`](requireNonEmptyString.md) instead. It expresses the same intent under the naming convention used across the library. This function is kept as-is for backwards compatibility and will be removed in a future major release.

```typescript
function nonEmptyString(value: unknown, name: string = "value"): string;
```

The older form of `requireNonEmptyString`, kept for the code that already calls it. Its second argument is the name to put in the message rather than the message itself, which is the opposite of every other guard here — that is why it was replaced.

## Parameters

| Parameter                       | Type      | Description                                                    |
| :------------------------------ | :-------- | :------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `value`                         | `unknown` | The value to validate.                                         |
| `name` _(optional)_ `= "value"` | `string`  | The argument name to put in the message. `"value"` by default. |

## Returns

`string` — the same string.

## Throws

| Exception                | Condition                                                   |
| :----------------------- | :---------------------------------------------------------- |
| `InvalidStringException` | the value is not a string, or holds nothing but whitespace. |

## Examples

### In use

```javascript
nonEmptyString("Data", "sheetName"); // => "Data"
```
